items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: The interviewee narrates stories about Jimmy Noon involving Sidney Bechet and Johnny Dodds (e.g., 'Sidney walked in... Jimmy Noon happened to come in... all three of them played at once'), but does not describe a direct personal interaction or relationship with Jimmy Noon himself.

ctx.x: But he was a marvelous clarinet player I think if he had stuck with the clarinet he would have

perhaps been the greatest. You know all the old-timers like Bunk once said he was the greatest and yeah around New Orleans he was like. Yeah around here they talk about even in Chicago there's one little story I'll tell you briefly Natty Dominic tells about when Johnny Dodds and Natty were playing at the Gallows 29 Club that would be in the late 30s even. Yeah. Evidently Sidney was with Noble Sissel. Noble Sissel yeah. And he came to town once Jimmy Noon happened to come in sitting at a table had his instrument…

reputation around New Orleans in the early days one of the things was that he never played a clarinet and when they played those rags in the Red Book they were written in in keys. Yeah mostly of them sharp keys. The players would would play like sharp keys six sharp something like that.
